s1.syndrome_frame: Acute liver injury with encephalopathy and coagulopathy
salient_findings: Markedly elevated liver enzymes (ALT 2869 U/L, AST 1469 U/L)
Elevated total bilirubin (15.1 mg/dL) and ammonia (55 μmol/L)
key_facts: 45-year-old woman from Mexico
Presented with headache and confusion
History of acute hepatitis A in Mexico one month prior
Normal vital signs on arrival
Altered mentation, icteric sclerae, jaundice, and asterixis on examination
Elevated liver enzymes (ALT 2869 U/L, AST 1469 U/L)
Elevated total bilirubin (15.1 mg/dL) and direct bilirubin (6.2 mg/dL)
Elevated INR (1.6) and ammonia (55 μmol/L)
MELD score of 22
Ferritin 1657 ng/mL and IgG 2580 mg/dL
Negative ANA, antimitochondrial antibody, antismooth muscle antibody, P-ANCA, C-ANCA, and anti–liver-kidney microsomal type 1 antibody
Normal ceruloplasmin and alpha-1 antitrypsin levels
Positive anti-HAV IgM, HEV IgG, and IgM, but undetectable HEV RNA
No use of herbal or alternative medicines
Abdominal ultrasound and CT scan showed no significant abnormalities

shortlist.label: Acute viral hepatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of acute hepatitis A and current presentation with elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin

shortlist.label: Autoimmune hepatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated IgG levels and presence of liver injury with encephalopathy and coagulopathy

shortlist.label: Wilson's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin, and presence of asterixis, which can be a sign of Wilson's disease

shortlist.label: Drug-induced liver injury
shortlist.why_kept: Although patient denied use of herbal or alternative medicines, this diagnosis cannot be entirely ruled out without further investigation

shortlist.label: Fulminant hepatic failure
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's MELD score of 22 and presence of encephalopathy and coagulopathy indicate severe liver dysfunction

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with altered mentation, icteric sclerae, jaundice, asterixis, and significantly elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels, along with an elevated INR and ammonia level, suggests severe liver dysfunction. The MELD score of 22 further supports the diagnosis of fulminant hepatic failure.

rejected.label: Acute viral hepatitis
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of acute hepatitis A and positive anti-HAV IgM, the current presentation and lab results suggest a more severe and acute liver injury than what is typically seen in acute viral hepatitis.

rejected.label: Autoimmune hepatitis
rejected.why: The negative results for ANA, antimitochondrial antibody, antismooth muscle antibody, and other autoantibodies make autoimmune hepatitis less likely.

rejected.label: Wilson's disease
rejected.why: Normal ceruloplasmin levels argue against Wilson's disease as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Drug-induced liver injury
rejected.why: The patient denied use of herbal or alternative medicines, and there is no other indication of drug use that could lead to liver injury.
